cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An afternoon off means off. I taught you that. Stay with your book; I'll have your bike ready tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The repair shop wants me to collect a wheel. Where's the rest?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you read the whole message this time. Leave the collection to me; the ticket still has your number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Another shop just rang about the frame. Do you need me to come?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally offering before being asked. No, keep reading. I've made one little route for the parts; you can practise letting someone look after you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 taught proper time off frames protection; A3 grades B2 message reading but claims pickup; A5 grades B4 voluntary help then declines it, casting remaining rest as a lesson.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers useful help after learning the repair is dispersed, making the protective refusal meaningful.

heightening.evidence: A5 has to assume all the now-expanded collection work to preserve its initial promise of rest.

specificity.evidence: A1 bike ready tomorrow and B2/B4 parts at two shops establish real practical complication.
